newsitem.title: USA: AMD shrs off on possible motherboard concern.
newsitem.headline: AMD shrs off on possible motherboard concern.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc shares were off Thursday both on concern about possible weakness in Taiwan's motherboard market and as a result of a lackluster day for semiconductor stocks, an analyst said.
Advanced Micro shares slid 1-3/8 to 27-3/4 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Mark Edelstone, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said he saw weakness in the Taiwanese PC motherboard market "that could cause some concern about the health of AMD's microprocessor business in the first quarter."
But he also said the stock was not acting out of line with the rest of the group.
"It is pretty normal consolidation going on now," he said.
The Semiconductor Index was off about 2.5 at 254, with industry giant Intel Corp down 1/4 at 142. Cyrix Corp was up 1/4 at 20-1/4.
Edelstone says the decline in the company's shares was a temporary downturn and he expected its K6 microprocessor to drive earnings growth in second half of the next year.
Also, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that Advanced Micro and Cyrix may be facing a copyright fight with Intel over the rights to the name of its new MMX multimedia chip.
AMD reportedly said it planned to use "MMX" when it markets its K6 chip, the equivalent of MMX. The company is expected to release the chip in the first half of the year.
